chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdul Hamid ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amru ibn Utbah narrated to us, from al-Husayn al-Ashqar, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umarah al-Kufi, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, say:

Whoever sheds a tear over us for blood that was spilled for our sake, or a right of ours that was diminished, or an honour that was violated against us or against any of our followers, Allah Most High shall settle him in Paradise for a long age.

بَوَّأَهُ.context: Divine placement in Paradise as reward

حُقُبًا.context: An extended period of time, indicating immense reward

دَمَعَتْ.context: The act of weeping as an expression of devotion and solidarity with Ahlul Bayt

سُفِكَ.context: Reference to the bloodshed suffered by Ahlul Bayt, especially at Karbala

شِيعَتِنَا.context: The Shia community who follow Ahlul Bayt

ai.seo_question: What reward does Imam al-Sadiq promise for those who weep over the sufferings of Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq promises divine reward in Paradise for anyone who weeps over the sufferings of the Ahlul Bayt. The hadith specifies three categories of injustice that merit such reward: bloodshed committed against them, rights that were usurped from them, and honour that was violated against them or their followers. This teaching, delivered in the context of early Shia communities who faced persecution, reinforced the spiritual significance of commemorating the tribulations of the Prophet's family and encouraged solidarity among their supporters.
